title: Telemetry Assertions & Fail-Forward Onboarding Playbook
author: Lena Ortiz
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a repeatable onboarding pattern for enterprise tenants that emphasizes telemetry-driven acceptance criteria and an explicit 'fail-forward' strategy when short-lived regressions are detected. The goal is to reduce friction for go-live while ensuring customers meet minimum SLOs, telemetry fidelity, and cost-guardrails before receiving production traffic allocation.

Intended audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs) and Onboarding Engineers
- SRE / Platform on-call for tenant cutovers
- Customer stakeholders for observability and FinOps

Goals:
- Define concrete telemetry assertions that must pass for tenant acceptance.
- Provide an operational runbook to ‘fail-forward’ (limit traffic, alert, and auto-mitigate) rather than immediate rollback for noncritical issues.
- Reduce false-positive rollbacks while protecting customer SLAs and Redwood capacity.

Scope and when to use this playbook:
- Used during enterprise onboarding, dedicated tenant cutover, and major model/telemetry contract changes.
- Not intended for full-production incident response (see escalation-playbook).

Prerequisites (must be satisfied before running):
1) Tenant has completed network and auth cutover (ingress gateway TLS validated, client certs, or API key handshake).
2) Telemetry Gatekeeper onboarding flow completed and sample payloads accepted (see integration guide).
3) Canary or staged traffic path created (e.g., 5–20% of expected peak) with routing rules in Routing Service (route id: onboarding/<tenant-id>).
4) Cost guardrails configured (quota-protector webhook, soft-limit notifications enabled).
5) Owners assigned: CSM (primary), SE (technical owner), Platform SRE on-call (escalation).

Roles & responsibilities:
- CSM: Customer-facing coordination and go/no-go decision based on playbook results.
- SE: Implements assertions, runs smoke tests, validates logs and traces.
- Platform SRE: Observability, alert tuning, and runbook execution for fail-forward actions.
- Customer Engineer: Provides buyer-side telemetry and acceptance signoff.

Telemetry assertions (minimum acceptance set):
The onboarding pipeline requires these assertions to be green for 30m steady-state during the canary window unless a documented exception is approved. All thresholds are tenant-scoped and recorded in the tenant onboarding ticket.

| Assertion | Signal | Threshold | Failure action (automatic) | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Request Success Rate | 2xx/(2xx+5xx+4xx) | >= 99% (5m rolling) | Reduce traffic to 10% route weight; alert SRE | SE/SRE |
| p95 Latency (generation) | latency_tokens_ms | <= 800ms | Pause batching; alert SE | SE |
| Token Cost Deviation | cost_per_1k_tokens | <= ±20% expected | Throttle per-tenant burst; notify CSM & FinOps | CSM/FinOps |
| Telemetry Completeness | percentage of requests with spans + token counts | >= 98% | Turn on telemetry sampling bypass and re-evaluate | SRE/SE |
| Embedding Index Lag | time_since_last_index_update | <= 10m (for streaming sync) | Fallback to read-only embedding index + alert | SE |
| Model Behavior Delta | eval-regression-score | no regression > 3% vs baseline | Quarantine model variant, fallback to baseline model | Product/SE |

Example CLI checks (smoke test snippets):
- Check success rate: redwoodctl tenant-metrics tail --tenant-id t123 --metric request_success_rate --window 5m
- Validate spans: redwoodctl traces find --tenant t123 --service ingress-gateway --min-samples 100

Fail-forward strategy (principles):
- Prioritize customer availability: prefer temporary traffic reduction, targeted throttling, or model fallback rather than full rollback of deployment.
- Alert early, automate low-impact mitigations, and require human escalation for persistent or safety-related failures.
- Capture actionable evidence automatically (request IDs, spans, sampled responses) to accelerate RCA.

Fail-forward runbook (step-by-step):
1) Detection: Alert fires on assertion breach. Pager includes metric snapshot, recent traces, and affected routes.
2) Initial triage (0–5 minutes): SE on-call reviews trace consistency and tokenization anomalies. If 1–2 noisy failures and telemetry incomplete -> run telemetry-bypass check (see snippet).
3) Automated mitigation (5–10 minutes): Platform automation performs one of the following, depending on the assertion:
   a) Reduce route weight: set route weight to min( current_weight * 0.25, 0.1 ) for 30 minutes.
   b) Apply model fallback: swap to pinned baseline model for the tenant via model-routing-policy.
   c) Enable sample-only telemetry bypass to surface missing spans.
4) Notification and decision (10–30 minutes): CSM and customer SME are notified with summary and recommended actions. If mitigations restore assertions -> monitor for 60 minutes then gradually increase weight in 3 steps (30m between each).
5) Escalation (30–90 minutes): If assertions remain degraded and customer SLA is at risk (success rate < 95% or p95 > 1500ms), trigger escalation-playbook to engage incident response and leadership.
6) Post-stabilization: If stable after step increases, run a scheduled synthetic test suite (see Section: Synthetics) and include results in QBR telemetry packet.

Automated mitigation rules (examples):
- success_rate_breach -> reduce_route_weight (duration: 30m, cooldown: 60m)
- latency_breach && model_variant != baseline -> apply_model_fallback (duration: 60m)
- telemetry_incomplete -> enable_bypass_sampling + mark_pull_request_for_client_instrumentation

Synthetics & acceptance tests (recommended):
- 30-minute tenant synthetic run: 1000 requests distributed over expected request types (embed/generate/chat). Capture traces, token counts, and exact responses.
- Behavioral smoke checks: run 20 eval prompts from customer-provided prompt set; compare automated scoring to baseline.

Communication templates (use in alerts/email to customer):
- Short alert subject: [Onboarding] Tenant t123: success_rate dropped to 96% (automated mitigation applied)
- Body: Include: what happened, immediate mitigation, expected customer impact (e.g., 10% reduced throughput), next steps, and POC contacts.

Acceptance signoff checklist (CSM to obtain):
- Telemetry assertions green for 30 minutes after mitigations reversed.
- Customer confirms in-product sampling/observability surface is visible and usable.
- FinOps confirms cost-projections within expected band and quota-protector hooks are registered.
- Legal/Compliance signoff (if restricted data flows required).

QBR and handoff artifacts to generate after go-live:
- Canary telemetry packet: include time-series of assertions, synthetic run output, failure-and-mitigation timeline.
- Action items: items requiring changes before ramp (instrumentation gaps, model test coverage, policy changes).
- Post-go-live stability window: 72 hours active monitoring with daily summaries to customer.

Operational notes & tips:
- Prefer model fallback to global rollback when the issue is domain-specific (model-behavior drift).
- Watch for tokenization edge-cases that cause apparent latency spikes; token-level traces are critical.
- Use the telemetry enrichment helper (redwoodctl telemetry enrich --tenant t123 --since 15m) to attach request metadata to alerts.

Appendix: Useful commands and JSON snippets
1) Route weight change (example API payload):
{
  "route_id": "onboarding/t123",
  "action": "set_weight",
  "weight": 0.1,
  "duration_minutes": 30
}
2) Model fallback toggle (example):
{
  "tenant_id": "t123",
  "from_model": "gptx-20b-v2",
  "to_model": "gptx-20b-baseline-v1",
  "apply_immediately": true
}
3) Telemetry completeness query (example):
redwoodctl metrics query --tenant t123 --metric telemetry_completeness --window 15m --group-by route

- Escalation-playbook (for high-severity or prolonged incidents)
